elements.element: Vendor provides post-termination transition assistance on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: 11.4: 'or upon any termination of this Agreement for any reason, M&I shall provide Customer ... all necessary assistance ... to facilitate the orderly transition of Services'

elements.element: Transition assistance available for up to 6 months
elements.evidence: 11.4: 'M&I shall continue to provide Customer all Services ... for a maximum period of six (6) months'
11.4: 'all Expenses and charges for Termination Assistance shall be computed in accordance with M&I's then-current rates'

elements.element: Return of Customer Data within 30 days of expiry/termination
elements.evidence: 11.5: 'within thirty (30) days following the Effective Date of Termination ... M&I shall return to Customer all Customer Data'

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format
elements.evidence: 11.5 uses 'in a commonly used, machine-readable format' rather than the playbook's express 'standard machine-readable format'

elements.element: Deletion of Customer Data after return
elements.evidence: 11.5: 'shall thereafter delete all Customer Data from its systems'
11.5: 'certify such deletion to Customer in writing'

elements.element: At least 90 days of transition assistance
elements.evidence: 11.4: 'for a maximum period of six (6) months' of continued Services plus transition assistance
11.5: 'within thirty (30) days following the Effective Date of Termination ... M&I shall return to Customer all Customer Data'

reasons: The inserted Section 11.5 supplies the missing data-return mechanic: 30-day return running from expiry/termination (not from a Customer request), followed by deletion and written certification — all preferred elements.

The format wording is 'commonly used, machine-readable format' rather than the playbook's 'standard machine-readable format'; per the official precision check this preferred sub-element is not expressly met, so the target level falls just short on wording only.
Fallback is fully satisfied: six months (well above 90 days) of transition assistance and export/return within 30 days.

Insertion is concise and confined to the absent obligation; no operative language in 11.4, 17.1 or 17.5 was altered, no undefined terms introduced, and the reference to 'Effective Date of Termination' and 'Termination Assistance period' ties to existing defined mechanics.
Optional tightening: change 'commonly used, machine-readable format' to 'standard, machine-readable format' to land squarely on the preferred position.
